data.gender_notes: Apfel is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Apfel derives from the German word for apple. In Western spiritual traditions, the apple symbolizes knowledge, temptation, and the Fall of Man. It is also a symbol of life, renewal, and fertility. The name Apfel carries the meaning “Fruit of knowledge and life” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Apfel usually hope their child will grow to embody fruit of knowledge and life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Apfel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fruit of knowledge and life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Apfel total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Apfel has its roots in Germanic culture, representing the German word for apple. Apples have been a significant fruit in German folklore and iconography. Apples are often featured in various folktales, as well as in poetic and artistic expressions. The name Apfel thus carries an association with the rich cultural heritage of Germany.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, the apple is a powerful symbol of knowledge, temptation, and the Fall of Man. The Bible recounts the story of Adam and Eve, in which they eat the forbidden fruit from the Tree of Knowledge, depicted as an apple in many artistic interpretations. This symbolizes mankind's departure from innocence and the entrance into knowledge, good and evil. Apfel, as a Christian name, carries the deeper spiritual significance of the trials and lessons embedded in this ancient story.
